body.statement: The law \(P_{\mathrm{ex}}\) in \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp} belongs to \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) for the displayed admissible constants and is nondegenerate: its responses have bounded nonzero conditional noise, its design point is interior, and its full stacked donor covariance is positive definite with nonzero off-diagonal entries. Let \(\bar e=(e_1^{\top},0,\ldots,0)^{\top}\in\mathbb R^{Sd}\). For every \(0<\delta\le\delta_0\), set \(u_\delta=\delta\Sigma\bar e/(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{1/2}\). Then \(\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_\delta\|_2=\delta\) and \(\bar e^{\top}u_\delta=\delta(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{1/2}>0\). Consequently, when \(\kappa=1\), the weighted surface has nonzero standardized gradient and its increment along \(u_\delta\) is \(\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{1/2}\delta/64+O(\delta^2)\); when \(0<\kappa<1\), the positive asymmetric-cusp increment is \(\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{\kappa/2}\delta^{\kappa}/64\). Hence \(\omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)\asymp\delta^{\kappa}\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\). This construction establishes non-vacuity only and does not derive the lower modulus for the general panel class.
body.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 a_0=\frac{\min\{B,L,1\}}{64},\qquad
 \bar e=(e_1^{\top},0,\ldots,0)^{\top}\in\mathbb R^{Sd},
 \qquad q_0=(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{1/2}.
\]
The positivity of \(B\) and \(L\) gives \(a_0>0\).  We first verify the covariance facts needed below.  From \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp},
\[
 \Sigma=\frac12I_{Sd}+\frac{1}{2Sd}\mathbf 1_{Sd}\mathbf 1_{Sd}^{\top}.
\]
The vector \(\mathbf 1_{Sd}\) is an eigenvector with eigenvalue one, while every vector orthogonal to it is an eigenvector with eigenvalue one half.  Thus \(\Sigma\) is positive definite, \(q_0>0\), and the restrictions \(c_\Sigma\le1/2\) and \(C_\Sigma\ge1\) in \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp} imply
\[
 c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}.
\]
This verifies \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}.  Every off-diagonal entry of \(\Sigma\) is \(1/(2Sd)>0\), so the claimed full-covariance nondegeneracy also holds.

We next verify the causal and support conditions.  At \(z_0=\tfrac12\mathbf 1_{Sd}\), both formulas for \(m_1\) in \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp} give \(m_1(z_{01})=4a_0\), and \(m_s(z_{0s})=4a_0\) for \(s>1\).  Hence
\[
 B_{si}(0)\in\{3a_0,5a_0\},
 \qquad B_{si}(1)=B_{si}(0)+a_0\in\{4a_0,6a_0\}.
\]
In particular, \(B_{si}(a)>0\) for \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and therefore \(R_{si0}(a)=B_{si}(a)-1>-1\).  By \texttt{def:buyhold-level} and the assignments \(W_{si,-1}=1\) and \(R_{sih}(a)=0\) for \(h>0\),
\[
 W_{si,-1}\prod_{h=0}^{H}\{1+R_{sih}(a)\}
 =1\cdot B_{si}(a)\prod_{h=1}^{H}1
 =B_{si}(a),
\]
where the last product is empty and equal to one when \(H=0\).  The prescribed equality \(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{si}(1)\) is \texttt{ass:consistency}.  Because \(\eta_{si}\) is centered and independent of \(z_0\),
\[
 \mathbb E[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]
 =m_s(z_{0s})+a_0\mathbb E[\eta_{si}\mid z_0]
 =m_s(z_{0s}),
\]
which is \texttt{ass:event-date-transport}.

For boundedness, when \(\kappa=1\), write \(y=x_1-1/2\).  Since \(-1/2\le y\le1/2\) and \(-1/4\le y+y^2\le3/4\),
\[
 \frac{15a_0}{4}\le m_1(x)\le\frac{19a_0}{4}.
\]
When \(0<\kappa<1\), the positive and negative parts in the formula for \(m_1\) cannot both be nonzero, and
\[
 \frac{7a_0}{2}\le m_1(x)\le5a_0.
\]
The remaining surfaces equal \(4a_0\).  Since all response noises take values in \(\{-1,1\}\), these bounds and the preceding event-outcome calculation yield
\[
 |Q_{sti}|\vee|B_{si}(0)|\vee|B_{si}(1)|
 \le6a_0
 \le\frac{6B}{64}<B.
\]
Thus \texttt{ass:bounded-wealth} holds.

It remains to verify \texttt{ass:holder-regression}.  If \(0<\lambda<1\), then \(\kappa=\lambda\).  The elementary inequality
\[
 |v_+^{\lambda}-w_+^{\lambda}|\le |v-w|^{\lambda}
\]
and its negative-part analogue show that the nonconstant part of \(m_1\) has \(\lambda\)-Holder seminorm at most \(a_0\) when two arguments are on the same side of \(x_1=1/2\).  If they are on opposite sides, each one-sided coordinate distance is at most the distance between the arguments, so the seminorm is at most \(3a_0/2\).  Consequently,
\[
 \|m_1\|_{\infty}+[m_1]_{\lambda}
 \le5a_0+\frac{3a_0}{2}<7a_0<L.
\]
If \(\lambda\ge1\), the selected surface is the quadratic surface, whose only possibly nonzero derivatives of positive order are
\[
 \partial_1m_1(x)=a_0\{1+2(x_1-1/2)\},
 \qquad \partial_{11}m_1(x)=2a_0.
\]
The first derivative is bounded by \(2a_0\) and is Lipschitz with constant \(2a_0\); the second derivative is bounded by \(2a_0\); and every derivative of order greater than two vanishes.  Under the stated integer-order convention, the usual isotropic Holder norm is therefore at most \(9a_0<L\) for every \(\lambda\ge1\).  Each constant surface has norm \(4a_0<L\).  This proves \texttt{ass:holder-regression}.  The selected first-cohort surface is non-affine because it has a nonzero quadratic term when \(\kappa=1\) and an asymmetric cusp when \(0<\kappa<1\).

The variables \(X_{st}\) are independent and uniform on \([0,1]^d\), so their common density is \(f_X(x)=1\).  Since \(c_X\le1\le C_X\), this is \texttt{ass:design-density}.  Moreover,
\[
 \operatorname{dist}(z_{0s},\partial[0,1]^d)=\frac12\ge\delta_0,
\]
which is \texttt{ass:interior-path}.  The product construction makes each cohort's calendar sequence independent across \(t\), although responses within a window share \(X_{st}\).  Hence its absolute-regularity coefficients satisfy
\[
 \beta(k)=0\le\beta_0\rho_0^k\qquad(k\ge1),
\]
verifying \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}.

Let \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{uv})_{1\le u\le S,\,1\le v\le T})\).  Independence and centering of the response noises give, for every \(s,t,i\),
\[
 \mathbb E[Q_{sti}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =m_s(X_{st})+a_0\mathbb E[\varepsilon_{sti}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =m_s(X_{st})
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =m_s(z_{0s})+a_0
 =\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].
\]
These are the two equalities in \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}.  Conditional on \((z_0,\mathcal X)\), the independent arrays \((\varepsilon_{sti},\eta_{si})\) make the unit histories mutually independent across \((s,i)\), which is \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence}.  The construction records each \(X_{st}\) itself as the training coordinate, proving \texttt{ass:center-only-design}.  The product-law independence of the donor Rademacher vectors from \(\mathcal X\), all response noises, and all event noises is \texttt{ass:donor-training-separation}.  The response law is nondegenerate because
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(Q_{sti}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)=a_0^2>0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(B_{si}(a)\mid z_0,\mathcal X)=a_0^2>0.
\]

Finally, the donor vectors \(U_j\) are independent and identically distributed with \(\mathbb E[U_j]=0\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(U_j)=I_{Sd}\).  Thus
\[
 \mathbb E[Z_j\mid z_0]=z_0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(Z_j\mid z_0)
 =\Sigma^{1/2}I_{Sd}\Sigma^{1/2}=\Sigma,
\]
which verifies \texttt{ass:donor-independence} and \texttt{ass:donor-unbiasedness}.  Also,
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\|_2^4\mid z_0\right]
 =\mathbb E[\|U_j\|_2^4]
 =(Sd)^2\le B^4,
\]
by the displayed restriction in \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp}; this is \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment}.  We have verified every member property in \texttt{def:panel-model-class}, and therefore
\[
 P_{\mathrm{ex}}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}.
\]

It remains to derive the local modulus; no lower-modulus premise is used.  For \(0<\delta\le\delta_0\), define
\[
 u_\delta=\frac{\delta\Sigma\bar e}{q_0}.
\]
Since \(q_0^2=\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e\),
\[
 \|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_\delta\|_2^2
 =\frac{\delta^2}{q_0^2}\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e
 =\delta^2,
 \qquad
 \bar e^{\top}u_\delta
 =\delta q_0>0.
\]
The radius restriction in \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp} gives
\[
 \|u_\delta\|_\infty
 \le\delta_0\|\Sigma\bar e/q_0\|_\infty
 \le\frac12.
\]
Since \(z_0=\tfrac12\mathbf 1_{Sd}\), it follows that \(z_0+u_\delta\in([0,1]^d)^S\).  Thus \(u_\delta\) is feasible in \texttt{def:local-modulus}.

Only the first coordinate of the first cohort contributes to the weighted increment.  If \(\kappa=1\), the stacked weighted gradient at \(z_0\) is \(\pi_1a_0\bar e\), whose covariance-standardized dual norm is
\[
 \|\Sigma^{1/2}(\pi_1a_0\bar e)\|_2
 =\pi_1a_0q_0>0.
\]
Substituting \(u_\delta\) gives the exact increment
\[
 \sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{m_s(z_{0s}+u_{\delta,s})-m_s(z_{0s})\}
 =\pi_1a_0(q_0\delta+q_0^2\delta^2)
 =\frac{\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}q_0}{64}\delta+O(\delta^2).
\]
It is in particular at least \(\pi_1a_0q_0\delta\).  If \(0<\kappa<1\), positivity of \(\bar e^{\top}u_\delta\) instead gives
\[
 \sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{m_s(z_{0s}+u_{\delta,s})-m_s(z_{0s})\}
 =\pi_1a_0q_0^\kappa\delta^\kappa
 =\frac{\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}q_0^\kappa}{64}\delta^\kappa.
\]
Therefore \texttt{def:local-modulus} implies
\[
 \omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)
 \ge \pi_1a_0\min\{q_0,q_0^\kappa\}\delta^\kappa.
\]

For the reverse inequality, let \(u\) be any feasible perturbation in \texttt{def:local-modulus}.  The upper ellipticity bound gives
\[
 \|u\|_2
 =\|\Sigma^{1/2}\Sigma^{-1/2}u\|_2
 \le C_\Sigma^{1/2}\delta.
\]
Put \(v=\bar e^{\top}u\).  Feasibility of \(z_0+u\) implies \(|v|\le1/2\).  If \(\kappa=1\),
\[
 |m_1(z_{01}+u_1)-m_1(z_{01})|
 =a_0|v+v^2|
 \le\frac32a_0|v|
 \le\frac32a_0C_\Sigma^{1/2}\delta.
\]
If \(0<\kappa<1\), the two branches of the asymmetric cusp give
\[
 |m_1(z_{01}+u_1)-m_1(z_{01})|
 \le a_0|v|^\kappa
 \le a_0C_\Sigma^{\kappa/2}\delta^\kappa.
\]
Every other cohort surface is constant, and \(0<\pi_1\le1\).  Taking the supremum over feasible \(u\) yields a finite constant \(C_{\mathrm{ex}}>0\), depending only on fixed class parameters, such that
\[
 \omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)\le C_{\mathrm{ex}}\delta^\kappa
 \qquad(0<\delta\le\delta_0).
\]
Together with the preceding positive lower bound, this proves
\[
 \omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)\asymp\delta^\kappa
 \qquad\text{as }\delta\downarrow0.
\]
Thus this bounded, noisy member of the base Holder panel class has the asserted attainable full-covariance modulus, while the argument makes no such assertion for an arbitrary member of that class.
body.justification: The explicit calculation exhibits a bounded noisy member of the base Holder panel class with a non-affine response surface and a sharp local modulus, without imposing a class-wide lower-modulus condition.
body.gap: The headline global frontier uses explicit worst-case witnesses and assumes no attainable direction for every law; this proposition separately records a concrete sensitive nondegenerate member rather than claiming that Holder smoothness alone implies attainability.
body.consumer: Referees can audit a legal bounded DGP with a sharp local modulus independently of the explicit witness families used for the headline donor converse.
